newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury issues final regulations on SLGS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury issues final regulations on SLGS.

text.p: The Treasury Department Monday issued final regulations for its state and local government series (SLGS) program designed to make it easier and less costly for these entities to refinance and invest proceeds from tax-exempt bonds.
These tax-exempt bonds are often issued to finance projects like school and road construction, bridge and tunnel repairs and the like.
The new regulations, which were proposed last July, will take effect later this week when published in the Federal Register and will apply to SLGS subscribed for from that date on.
Included among the changes are a 60 percent reduction in fees from 12.5 to 5.0 basis points, shortened notice periods for purchase and early redemption.
The department said it did add some regulatory language based on comments including an increase in SLGS maturities to as much as 40 years from the current 30 years.
It also will allow a tax-exempt issuer to lock in a given days's SLGS rate with the postmark on the subscription. The rules clarified penalty and revocation rules as well.
Treasury later said the new regulations would be effective Monday Oct 28.
